questions.prompt: You start a task in Claude Code on the web. What code does it work on?

options.text: Your laptop's working tree, streamed to the cloud
A fresh clone of your connected repo in Anthropic's cloud — your uncommitted local changes are not there
A cached copy from your last local session
It can't touch code; the web tier is chat only

questions.explanation: The web tier runs on cloud infrastructure against a fresh clone. That's what makes machine-off work possible — and why uncommitted local changes are invisible to it; results come back as branches or PRs.

options.text: Moves your session to Anthropic's cloud
Lets Claude control your mouse and keyboard
Generates a QR pairing code so a browser or phone can attach to your RUNNING LOCAL session — same working tree, steered from another device
Creates a read-only share link of the transcript

questions.explanation: Remote Control relocates your hands, not the session: the work still happens on your machine against your files. Cloud execution (a) is the separate web tier.

questions.prompt: What does --resume carry forward when you pick a session back up?

options.text: The session's accumulated context — conversation, decisions, progress — so you continue where it left off instead of starting cold
Nothing; it just reopens an empty window with the same title

questions.explanation: The session is the durable artifact; surfaces (CLI, web, phone) are windows onto it. Resuming restores its context — which is also why module 10's hygiene matters: you resume the rot along with the progress.
